title: Iterator vs Iterable
summary: What each interface is for, why Iterable forces you to implement Iterator, and why the JDK collections are built this way.

title: Pattern Matching
summary: How instanceof, switch, and record patterns let you test an object's structure and extract its data in one step, instead of casting after a type check.

references.label: Pattern Matching — Java SE 26 Language Guide

title: The Collection Interface
summary: The generic root interface of the Collections Framework — what add, remove, and bulk operations guarantee, and why several of them can throw at runtime instead of failing to compile.

references.label: Collections Framework Overview — The Java Tutorials

title: The List Interface
summary: How List builds a positional, duplicate-allowing sequence on top of Collection — indexed access, sublists, sort, and the unmodifiable lists produced by List.of().

title: The Set Interface
summary: How Set forbids duplicates, how SortedSet and NavigableSet layer ordering and closest-match lookups on top of it, and why their range views are backed by the original set.

title: The Queue Interface
summary: Why Queue defines two parallel families of methods — one that throws on failure, one that reports it — and what that means for empty and fixed-length queues.

title: The Deque Interface
summary: How Deque extends Queue into a double-ended queue that can also act as a stack, and how its addFirst/addLast, peek, and remove families each split into a throwing and a reporting version.

title: Generics: Bounded Types, Wildcards, and Erasure
summary: How parameterized types move casts and type-mismatch checks from runtime to compile time, what bounded types and PECS wildcards (extends/super) actually constrain, and why erasure means there's really only one class file per generic type at runtime.

references.label: Java Language Specification — Chapter 4.5, Parameterized Types

title: Records and Sealed Types
summary: How a record turns a data-holder class into one line (canonical/compact constructors, free equals/hashCode/toString, shallow immutability), and how sealed classes/interfaces replace "anyone can extend this" with an explicit, exhaustive permits list — the pairing that makes closed hierarchies safe to model.

references.label: Java SE Language Documentation — Record Classes
Java SE Language Documentation — Sealed Classes and Interfaces

title: Comparators and Collection Algorithms
summary: How Comparator decouples ordering from a type entirely (unlike the one fixed Comparable.compareTo()), how comparing()/thenComparing() build multi-key comparators without a hand-written compare(), and what the static algorithms on Collections (sort, shuffle, unmodifiable/synchronized/checked views) actually guarantee.

title: HttpClient: The Modern java.net.http API
summary: How HttpClient's builder pattern replaced HttpURLConnection's low-level, awkward API — synchronous send() vs. asynchronous sendAsync() returning a CompletableFuture, and how BodyHandlers decides what shape the response body arrives in.

title: Regular Expressions with Pattern and Matcher
summary: Why Pattern.compile() and Matcher exist as two separate objects (compile once, match many), the difference between find()/matches()/lookingAt(), and how capturing groups — numbered and named — pull substrings out of a match instead of just testing yes/no.
